nodes.label: Can systematic computational search map spacetime solution space?
nodes.summary: The project's methodological research question. It does not presume a transportation shortcut exists.

nodes.label: Search may outperform isolated manual proposal
nodes.summary: A reproducible search policy may classify or identify scientifically interesting regions more efficiently than a defined naive baseline.

nodes.label: Earth to Mars benchmark
nodes.summary: Mars is a motivating benchmark and communication frame, not a claim that the project can alter travel today.

nodes.label: Flat spacetime baselines
nodes.summary: Simple metrics used to verify that the pipeline handles established mathematics before exploring novelty.

nodes.label: Minkowski baseline
nodes.summary: The standard constant flat-spacetime metric in Cartesian coordinates.

nodes.label: Scoped Minkowski benchmark validator
nodes.summary: Exact arithmetic checks for the Cartesian baseline and one declared constant linear coordinate map.

nodes.label: Baseline deterministic verification run
nodes.summary: Twelve implemented checks passed using exact arithmetic and scoped analytic implications.

nodes.label: The stored baseline metric is exactly flat in its declared scope
nodes.summary: Supported by the versioned baseline validator and exact committed artifact. Not independently reproduced yet.

nodes.label: Independent reproduction requested
nodes.summary: An outside contributor should rerun the baseline from a clean clone and compare the fingerprint.

nodes.label: No learned search policy deployed
nodes.summary: The project has not trained or promoted any model. Benchmarks and data governance come first.

nodes.label: Rescaled-coordinate Minkowski benchmark
nodes.summary: The same flat spacetime expressed through one declared constant linear coordinate map.

nodes.label: Coordinate-equivalence verification run
nodes.summary: Fourteen preregistered checks passed using exact pullback arithmetic.

nodes.label: Two submitted component grids describe the same scoped flat geometry
nodes.summary: Supported only for the exact declared constant linear map and separately checked inside this repository.

edges.summary: The research question is tested through a methodological hypothesis.
The Mars benchmark makes the abstract research question concrete.
The candidate is a flat-spacetime baseline.
The run evaluates the committed candidate document.
The run records the validator identity and version.
The claim is narrower than and directly traceable to the run output.
A future versioned search policy will be compared with a naive baseline.
The second candidate is another representation of the established flat-spacetime family.
The run evaluates the committed rescaled-coordinate candidate.
The run uses the exact linear-coordinate profile of the deterministic validator.
The coordinate-equivalence claim is limited to and traceable to the preregistered run.
